brief: Depends on b11's season(). The courtyard is what this piece is named after, the loop has not touched it in nine iterations, and it is the most static part of the town precisely because it is the best built: the CA ring, dieback, daisies, desire paths and ivy all arrive at their maturity-1 state and then hold there forever. Let the planting CA read the season — growth rate, the bloom stage a bed is able to reach, and the dieback term all scale with it, so the beds fill and empty over the cycle instead of saturating and stopping. The lawn colour and the gatehouse ivy should follow the same scalar rather than deriving their own. This is the reader that makes b11 worth having: a season you can only see in the sky is a lighting change.
successLooksLike: Two screenshots of the same courtyard half a cycle apart are obviously two different pictures — one in full bloom, one bare and turned over — and a per-day sample of the census's blooming count traces a curve instead of a plateau.
avoid: If b11 did not land, do NOT invent a second seasonal scalar to work around it — log this brief as blocked and take the next one. Do not add a species. Do not special-case the ring; roofs are emergent and so is the bed ring. Heed the CA-variety law: a rule that empties the beds coherently will also make them monotonous over several cycles unless something reseeds the mix, so measure variety across cycles and not just within one. And the courtyard must never read as dead — a bare bed still has structure.
